\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{प्राप्नोति} (prāpnoti)}{प्राप्नोति (prāpnoti)}]{\sk{प्राप्नोति} (prāpnoti) — reaches, obtains}

\label{lesson:SA-C136-prapnoti}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for climbs, then the Sanskrit for climbs down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{प्राप्नोति}}
\textbf{\sk{प्राप्नोति}} — \emph{prāpnoti} — \textquotedblleft{}reaches, obtains\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{prāpnoti} comes from \emph{pra} \textquotedblleft{}forward\textquotedblright{} and the root √āp \textquotedblleft{}reach, obtain\textquotedblright{} (MW; CDIAL 8947): \textquotedblleft{}reaches forward to, attains\textquotedblright{}. MW compares √āp with Latin \emph{apiscor} \textquotedblleft{}reach\textquotedblright{} and \emph{aptus}, the source of English \emph{apt}; Gujarati kept it as \emph{pāmvũ} \textquotedblleft{}to obtain\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8947).
\end{cousinweb}

\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{धारयति} (dhārayati)}{धारयति (dhārayati)}]{\sk{धारयति} (dhārayati) — wears, holds}

\label{lesson:SA-C136-dharayati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for climbs down, then the Sanskrit for reaches.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{धारयति}}
\textbf{\sk{धारयति}} — \emph{dhārayati} — \textquotedblleft{}wears, holds\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{dhārayati} is the causative form of the root √dhṛ \textquotedblleft{}hold, bear, support\textquotedblright{}, and in practice the usual present (MW; CDIAL 6791). The root is inherited from Indo-European (EtymDB), and \emph{dharma}, \textquotedblleft{}what holds things up\textquotedblright{}, comes from it too. Hindi kept it as \emph{dhārnā} \textquotedblleft{}to hold, owe\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6791).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{गणयति} (gaṇayati)}{गणयति (gaṇayati)}]{\sk{गणयति} (gaṇayati) — counts}

\label{lesson:SA-C136-ganayati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for reaches, then the Sanskrit for wears.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{गणयति}}
\textbf{\sk{गणयति}} — \emph{gaṇayati} — \textquotedblleft{}counts\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{gaṇayati} \textquotedblleft{}counts, reckons\textquotedblright{} appears from the Mahābhārata on. CDIAL 3993, after J. C. Wright, suggests it grew from a Middle Indic form of \emph{gṛṇ-} \textquotedblleft{}address, praise\textquotedblright{}, so its origin is uncertain. It lives on as Hindi \emph{ginnā} \textquotedblleft{}to count\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 3993).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{मार्जयति} (mārjayati)}{मार्जयति (mārjayati)}]{\sk{मार्जयति} (mārjayati) — wipes, cleans}

\label{lesson:SA-C136-marjayati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for wears, then the Sanskrit for counts.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{मार्जयति}}
\textbf{\sk{मार्जयति}} — \emph{mārjayati} — \textquotedblleft{}wipes, cleans\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{mārjayati} is the causative form of the root √mṛj \textquotedblleft{}wipe, rub, clean\textquotedblright{} (MW). MW sets √mṛj beside Latin \emph{mulgere} \textquotedblleft{}to milk\textquotedblright{} and English \emph{milk}. The plain verb \emph{mārjati} lives on as Gujarati \emph{mājvũ} \textquotedblleft{}to scour\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10080).
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\sk{बध्नाति} (badhnāti)}{बध्नाति (badhnāti)}]{\sk{बध्नाति} (badhnāti) — ties}

\label{lesson:SA-C136-badhnati}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Sanskrit for counts, then the Sanskrit for wipes.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \sk{बध्नाति}}
\textbf{\sk{बध्नाति}} — \emph{badhnāti} — \textquotedblleft{}ties\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{badhnāti} comes from the root √bandh \textquotedblleft{}bind, tie\textquotedblright{}, in its Rigvedic class-9 form (CDIAL 9133). MW sets √bandh beside Gothic \emph{bindan} and English \emph{bind}, and the other present \emph{bandhati} lives on as Hindi \emph{bāṁdhnā} \textquotedblleft{}to tie\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 9139).
\end{cousinweb}
